pride_data.title: Characterization of microbe-containing phagosomes using APEX2-based proximity labeling
pride_data.projectDescription: Phagocytosis is the process by which myeloid phagocytes bind and internalize potentially dangerous microbes. During phagocytosis, innate immune receptors and the associated signaling adapters are localized to the maturing phagosome compartment. We used proximity labeling of phagosomal contents (PhagoPL) to identify proteins localizing to phagosomes containing model yeast and bacteria and identified programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) as a protein that specifically enriches in phagosomes containing yeast. We found that PD-L1 directly binds to yeast upon processing in phagosomes and influences production of a subset of inflammatory cytokines and chemokines produced when macrophages encounter yeast.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: APEX2-based PhagoPL BMDMs were seeded into 6-well-plates and primed overnight with 10 ng/ml mouse granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF, PeproTech). The following day, cells were washed once with D-PBS. Opti-MEM media (Gibco) with 500 μM biotin-phenol (Sigma) and AEPX2-expressing microbes were added to the cells and the plates were centrifuged at 500g for 1 min before being incubated at 37°C to allow for 30 min of microbe phagocytosis by macrophages. The number of AEPX2-expressing microbes added was titrated in pilot experiments to ensure equal levels of total biotinylated protein determined by immunoblotting. At the end of incubation, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG, Sigma) was added to 200 μM and 1 mM H2O2 was quickly added to initiate APEX2 labeling. After 1 min of labeling at room temperature (RT), cells were sequentially washed 3 times with quenching solution (10 mM sodium ascorbate, 5 mM Trolox and 10 mM sodium azide in D-PBS), 3 times with D-PBS, and lysed with 1% SDS lysis buffer (1% SDS, 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 10 mM EDTA). Lysates were boiled at 95°C for 10 min and clarified by centrifugation at 12000g for 10 min at 4°C. 3 independent biological replicates were prepared for each of the microbes.  Preparation of APEX2-labeled proteins for mass spectrometry Streptavidin magnetic beads (Pierce) were washed with 0.05% SDS lysis buffer (0.05% SDS, 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 10 mM EDTA). Lysates from APEX2-labled cell samples were diluted 1:20 into Tris-HCl buffer (50 mM Tris, pH7.5) and incubated with the washed beads for 90 min at RT with gentle mixing. Proteins bound to streptavidin beads were sequentially washed twice with 0.05% SDS lysis buffer, once with 1 M KCl, once with 0.1 M Na2CO3, once with 2 M urea in 10 mM Tris-HCl, once with 3 M urea in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate (ABC) buffer and once with 50 mM ABC buffer. Washed beads were resuspended in 50 mM ABC buffer and the bead-bound proteins were reduced with Bond-BreakerTM TCEP solution (5 mM, Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 55°C for 30 min. The samples were alkylated with 10 mM iodoacetamide (Sigma) for 20 min in the dark at 25°C with shaking. The reaction was then quenched upon adding DTT (20 mM final). The beads were subsequently washed twice with 2 M Urea in 50 mM ABC buffer before being digested overnight at 37°C with trypsin in 2 M urea (50 mM ABC buffer).  Label-free Proteomic Analysis Label-free proteomic comparison was conducted essentially as described (Yan et al., 2022). For each sample, 14 μL tryptic peptide solution was loaded onto a 2-cm trap column and then separated on a 50-cm EASY-Spray analytical column (Thermo Scientific) heated to 55°C, using a 3-h gradient at the flow rate of 250 nL/min. The resolved peptides were ionized by an EASY-Spray ion source (Thermo Scientific). Precursor and fragment mass spectra were acquired in a data-dependent manner in an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific). EASY-IC was used for internal mass calibration. Precursor ion scans were acquired in 240,000 resolution at m/z of 400 Th, with an ion packet setting of 4 × 105 for automatic gain control and a maximum injection time of 250 milliseconds (ms). Most intense peptide ions with charge state of 2-7 and mass-to-charge ratios of 375-1,650 were automatically selected for fragmentation by higher energy collisional dissociation, using 30% normalized collision energy. Tandem mass spectra were acquired in the ion trap, using rapid ion trap scan at 1 × 104 automatic gain control and a maximum injection time of 35 ms. To minimize redundant data acquisition, dynamic exclusion was enabled (repeat count of 1, exclusion during of 60s, and repeat during of 60s).
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: The acquired data (18 RAW files) were searched against the a concatenated database consisting of E. coli (BL21DE3), mouse (C57BL/6J), Saureus (NCTC8325), and S. cerevisiae (ATCC204508) protein sequences,  using MaxQuant (v1.5.5.1) (Cox and Mann, 2008). The searching parameters were set as follows: trypsin/P as the protease; carbamidomethyl (C) as fixed modification; oxidation (M), acetyl (protein N-term), and deamidation (NQ) as variable modifications; minimal peptide length as 7; up to two missed cleavages; mass tolerance for precursor ions was 4.5 ppm and for fragment ions was 0.5 Da; identification of second peptides enabled; label free quantification enabled, with match-between-runs within 1 min. A standard false discovery rate of 0.01 was used to filter peptide-spectrum matches, peptide identifications, and protein identifications.
